title: OpenWrt SQM Latency Under Load
app: OpenWrt, UniFi, Pi-hole, AdGuard Home, Tailscale, Cloudflare Tunnel, DNS over HTTPS resolvers, and scheduled probes via syslog, APIs, and Splunk HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=openwrt:syslog event=sqm_test
| stats avg(latency_under_load_ms) as avg_latency_ms, max(latency_under_load_ms) as max_latency_ms by router
| where avg_latency_ms>50 OR max_latency_ms>100
| sort - avg_latency_ms
description: Uses OpenWrt SQM measurements telemetry to monitor latency while the link is under load in index=personal.
value: Splunk turns the feed into an operational check for bufferbloat returning despite shaping, so the signal does not stay buried inside separate consumer apps or exports.
implementation: Ingest OpenWrt SQM measurements data through its real API, export, MQTT bridge, or open-source connector into `index=personal`; preserve the fields referenced in the SPL and schedule the search on a hourly cadence.
visualization: Router table of average and max under-load latency.
grandmaExplanation: It highlights latency while the link is under load so you can spot bufferbloat returning despite shaping before it becomes annoying.
